texts.preamble: Somla Naik vs Manjunath S on 1 April, 2026 Kabc020241662024 Before The Court Of 10th Additional Small Causes And Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, At: Bengaluru (Scch-16) Present: Sri. Mohammed Yunus Athani B.A.,Ll.B., X Addl. Judge, Court of Small Causes & Member, Mact, Bengaluru. Mvc No.3605/2024 Dated this 1st day of April, 2026 Petitioner: Somla Naik S/o Rama Naik, Aged about 55 years, R/at No.93, Venkateshapura Tanda, Gurusiddapura Post, Jagalur Taluk, Davanagere - 577 513. Also R/at No.212, 2nd Floor, 1st Cross, 3rd Main, Peenya 2nd Stage, Bengaluru. (Sri K. S. Nagaraja, Advocate) Vs. Respondents: 1. Manjunath S. S/o Sharanappa, R/at No.18, Gowdagere, Horakere, Jagalur Town, Davanagere-577528. 2 (Rc owner of the water tanker bearing No.KA-17-TD-2353) (Sri Ningaraja E., Advocate) Somla Naik vs Manjunath S on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7377407/ 1 2. The General Manager, Icici Lombard Gen. Ins. Co. Ltd., Motor Claims Hub, No.121, 9th Floor, The Estate, Dickenson Road, M.G. Road, Bengaluru - 560 001. (Policy No.3008/241308407/02/000, date of validity from 04-03-2024 to 03-03-2025) (Sri V. R. Muralidhara, Advocate) Judgment
texts.facts: This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- from the respondents, for the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident. 2. The brief facts of the case are as follows: On 01-05-2024 at about 10.45 a.m., the petitioner was riding the TVS XL Moped bearing No.KA-17-HG-0707, slowly, cautiously, by observing all traffic rules and regulations, near Kere Koodi Basavanna Temple, Jagalur-Kottur road, Jagalur Town, Davanagere. At that time, all of a sudden a water tanker bearing No.KA-17-TD-2353, which was driven by its driver with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, came from opposite direction and dashed against the TVS XL Moped of the petitioner. Due to the said impact, the petitioner has fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over his body. Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Government Hospital, Jagalur, wherein he took first aid treatment and then he was shifted to Puttur Hospital, Hosapete, wherein he took treatment as an inpatient. Earlier to the accident, he was working as mason and was earning Rs.1,200/- per day. But, due to the accidental injuries, he has become permanently disabled and thereby lost his earning capacity. The Jagalur Police have registered the case against the driver of the said water tanker for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 338 of I.P.C. The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle. Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner. Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest. 3. On service of notice to the respondents, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsel and filed their separate written statements. 4. The respondent No.1 in his written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition. He has contended that, the petitioner was riding the motorcycle in a rash and negligent manner, Somla Naik vs Manjunath S on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7377407/ 2 without following traffic rules and caused the alleged accident. But, the petitioner colluding with the jurisdictional police has lodged a false case and filed a false charge-sheet against the driver of water tanker bearing No.KA-17-TD-2353, with an intention to have illegal gain. If this Hon'ble Court come to a conclusion that the petitioner is entitled for compensation, the respondent No.2 insurance is solely responsible to pay compensation to the petitioner. Hence, the present claim petition is liable to be dismissed against respondent No.1. For the above denials and contentions, he has prayed to dismiss the petition. 5. Whereas, respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied all the allegations made in the petition. It has admitted the issuance of insurance policy bearing No.3008/241308407/02/000 in favour of respondent No.1, in respect of water tanker bearing No.KA-17-TD-2353 and its validity, subject to terms and conditions, exceptions, limits and endorsement of the policy and subject to compliance of 64-VB of Insurance Act. 6. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the sides, the following issues are framed:
texts.arguments: Further it is contended that, in the alleged accident the petitioner has not sustained injury and the petitioner colluding with the hospital authorities has got created additional medical bills with a sole intention to get more compensation from this respondent. Further it is contended that, as on the date of accident he had valid vehicle documents and his vehicle was insured by the respondent No.2 insurance company and the same was valid from 04-03- 2024 to 03-03-2025. The permit, driving licence and other documents were also in force. Further it is contended that, the petition is bad for non-compliance of provision under Section 134(c) of Motor Vehicles Act. Further it is contended that, the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties, the owner and insurer of motorcycle bearing No.KA-17-HG-707 which involved in the alleged accident, they are also proper and necessary parties to the present proceedings to adjudicate the controversy involved in the case. It has denied the occurrence, mode of the accident and involvement of vehicle bearing No.KA-17-TD-2353 as alleged in the claim petition. Further it is contended that, after lapse of 2 days the petitioner has filed a false case against the said vehicle to cause wrongful loss to this respondent. Further it is contended that, the respondent No.1 has willfully entrusted his vehicle to a person who did not possess valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident and allowed him to ply the said vehicle on the road without having valid and effective permit, fitness certificate and converting the vehicle illegally as water tanker, as against its authorization. The respondent No.1 has committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy and also violation of Section 150(2) of Amended Motor Vehicles Act, 2019. Therefore, this respondent is not liable to pay the compensation in view of amended provision of Motor Vehicle Act, with effect from 01-04-2022, in the above matter. Further it is contended that, the alleged accident has not occurred in the manner as pleaded by the petitioner. The alleged accident is caused due to rash and negligent riding of the motorcycle by the petitioner and he has attributed more contributory negligence in the cause of accident. Further, he was riding the motorcycle without holding driving licence, insurance policy and without wearing safety head gear. Thus, he being guilty of violation of motor vehicle rules and regulations, is not entitled to seek for compensation from this respondent. There was no rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the water tanker. It has denied the age, income and avocation of the petitioner, injuries sustained, medical expenses and treatment taken by him. The compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant. For the above denials and contentions, it is prayed to dismiss the petition. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Ravi V/s Badrinarayan and others, reported in (2011) 4 SCC 693, has clearly held that, "the delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt claimant's case in genuine cases. In Indian conditions, it is not expected that a person would to rush to police station after accident. The kith and kin of victim are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging FIR. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011) Somla Naik vs Manjunath S on 1 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7377407/ 6 11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof in a criminal case are not required." 19. The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Bimla Devi and others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SCC 513, has clearly held that, "in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are merely required to establish their case on touch stone of preponderance of probability and the standard of proof on beyond reasonable doubt could not be applied." 20. 24. As per the ratio laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others V/s Delhi Transport Corporation and another, reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, the appropriate multiplier for a person whose is aged about 55 years is 11. Therefore, loss of future income is Total annual income X disability/100 X multiplier = Rs.1,98,000 X 15/100 X 11 = Rs.3,26,700/-. 25. Medical expenses: The petitioner has deposed that, he has incurred expenses of Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical, conveyance, nourishment and other incidental charge etc. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,76,341/- towards the medical expenses.
